subject: Lockstep renewal: short-term rate shelter & commit options
messages:
From: Carol Morton <carol.morton@lockstepanalytics.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: legal@lockstepanalytics.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:43 -0700
Subject: Renewal: request for short-term rate shelter & commit options

Vanessa —

Thanks for the partnership this past year. We’re preparing our renewal and have an operational spike that’s making next quarter’s budget look ugly. Two asks from my side: 1) can Redwood hold current effective rates for a short runway (we’re asking 8–12 weeks) while we finalize product spend approvals, and 2) what commit/credit structure would you propose if we increase committed capacity to cover the expected run rate?

Background: we expect a transient 2.5x token volume for 6 weeks and then still land ~1.3x of our current run rate for the remainder of year 1. We’d rather avoid a full reprice mid-quarter. We’ve attached a one-page summary of projected usage and the current invoice history.

Ideal outcome for Lockstep: preserve current per-token blended rate for 8 weeks, receive a modest credit/smoothing mechanism for the immediate overage, and negotiate a 12‑month renewal with a stepped commit target (1.2x year-1 baseline, with an option to true-up).

Can you share a short options matrix we can take to our CFO + legal this week? We’re targeting a renewal signature by 9/24.

Thanks —
Carol Morton
VP Finance, Lockstep Analytics
carol.morton@lockstepanalytics.com
Attachment: Lockstep_Renewal_Request_2027.pdf (1 page)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Carol Morton <carol.morton@lockstepanalytics.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 11:03:17 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: request for short-term rate shelter & commit options

Carol —

Appreciate the context and the clear targets. I pulled together three pragmatic options that balance Lockstep’s need for a short-term rate shelter while protecting Redwood’s unit economics. Attached is a one-page options summary (Redwood-OptionSummary-vanessa_20270914.pdf). High level: 

- Option A — 8-week full rate hold (current blended rate) + 20% committed uplift for 12 months. We provide a one-time overage smoothing credit equal to 15% of projected spike spend, applied to the first invoice after the spike. Requires signed addendum to existing SOW and renewal by 9/24.

- Option B — 12-week partial hold (75% of current blend) + 10% committed uplift + 30-day amortized credit for overage. Less aggressive from Redwood’s side, longer runway for Lockstep.

- Option C — No rate hold; accelerated commit discount schedule: 5% off list for first 6 months if Lockstep increases committed capacity 1.5x and commits for 12 months. We can combine with token-based burst credits.

Next steps I recommend: 1) confirm which option you prefer, 2) legal reviews the addendum (I can loop Redwood legal), 3) we schedule a 30-min alignment call tomorrow to lock terms and timeline. If you prefer, I can pre-authorize the addendum so legal just fills in standard clauses — expedites signature.

Happy to hop on a call this afternoon.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Attachment: Redwood-OptionSummary-vanessa_20270914.pdf (1 page)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 13:00:05 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal: request for short-term rate shelter & commit options

Team — forwarding Lockstep’s ask and the options I outlined below. They want a fast yes/no to take to CFO/legal (deadline 9/24). Points I want you on: 

- Tradeoff guidance: which option best preserves gross margin while offering a defensible concession? I think Option A is acceptable if we 1) require a minimum 20% committed uplift and 2) make the overage smoothing a one-time credit (15% as proposed).
- Operational impact: Marcus, any red flags for capacity planning if they spike 2.5x for 6 weeks and then land at 1.3x? Do we need to reserve Dedicated pool capacity or can routing/burst cover?
- Approval ask: Ben — can you greenlight Option A with the proposed credit and require the signed addendum by 9/24? If not, what conditions would you add (term extension, staged true-up, or higher commit)?

Quoted for context: 
> On Tue, 14 Sep 2027 11:03:17 -07:00, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> 
> Carol —
> 
> Appreciate the context and the clear targets. I pulled together three pragmatic options that balance Lockstep’s need for a short-term rate shelter while protecting Redwood’s unit economics. Attached is a one-page options summary. High level: 
> 
> - Option A — 8-week full rate hold (current blended rate) + 20% committed uplift for 12 months. We provide a one-time overage smoothing credit equal to 15% of projected spike spend, applied to the first invoice after the spike. Requires signed addendum to existing SOW and renewal by 9/24.

Thanks —
Vanessa

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 15:38:11 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal: request for short-term rate shelter & commit options

Vanessa —

Agree with moving forward on Option A with guardrails. Approve with the following conditions: 

1) Signed addendum covering the 8-week rate hold must be executed by 2027-09-24 (puts pressure on Lockstep; we can offer a one-week grace but no longer).
2) The 20% committed uplift must be explicit in the SOW (minimum committed tokens per month). We will include a staged true-up: if actual post-spike usage < 90% of the uplift for 3 consecutive months, Lockstep can reduce commitment by up to 10% at the 6-month mark.
3) Over-usage smoothing credit is capped at $75k (financial protection). We apply the credit to the first invoice after the spike and it is non-recurring.
4) Redwood legal will prepare a short addendum (SOW-Addendum-D48321.docx). Vanessa, please send the addendum request to legal@redwoodinference.com and loop Lockstep legal.

Marcus — please confirm capacity plan — if we need to reserve Dedicated pool time, flag cost delta. Monica — once legal drafts the addendum, coordinate the signature path on the HubSpot deal and make sure renewal milestone is updated.

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

---
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 15:41:02 -07:00
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal: request for short-term rate shelter & commit options

Short note: we can absorb the 6‑week spike without moving to Dedicated if we throttle routing and temporarily scale burst capacity in region us-west-2. Cost delta is manageable within the one-time credit Ben outlined; I’ll build a simple runbook for ops and share by EOD. No blockers on my side.

Marcus Lin
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
